content.overview: A strong irrigation handoff states what the system was commanded to do, what was actually delivered, where the discrepancy occurred, what root-zone effect followed and where the responder's authority ends.

vocabulary.definition: Evidence that intended irrigation volume or flow physically reached representative points.
The point at which evidence supports a fault class but not the internal mechanical cause.
Transfer of evidence to the role authorized to inspect or repair protected irrigation equipment.

sections.title: Connect command to physical delivery
sections.body: Record zone command/runtime, measured emitter output, pressure observations and affected positions. A controller log alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Include root-zone consequence
sections.body: Dryback, moisture or EC patterns can show whether the delivery fault materially affected crop conditions.

sections.title: Escalate without prescribing protected repair
sections.body: Identify the suspected fault class and safe checks completed, then route pump, electrical, pressure-system or protected disassembly work to qualified personnel.

workedExamples: A handoff states that Zone 3 far-end emitters averaged 45% less output with lower measured pressure and faster dryback; it does not instruct an unqualified worker to dismantle the pump.
commonMistakes: Giving protected repair instructions from an operational role.
content.practicalApplication: Write an irrigation fault handoff from a supplied controller log, pressure readings, emitter catches and root-zone trend.
content.summary: Good irrigation escalation translates measurements into a bounded fault class and preserves safe service boundaries.
